Monkey nuts are a food item, healing 4 hitpoints when eaten. They can be purchased at Solihib's Food Stall on Ape Atoll after starting the Monkey Madness I quest. Players who have not completed Monkey Madness II must be in the form of a monkey (by holding any monkey greegree ) before talking to the stall owner or they will be thrown in jail just like in the quest. A M'speak amulet is not required in order to buy from Solihib's shop.

5 Monkey nuts are also used in farming , together with a monkey bar and a ground Suqah tooth , as the payment for protecting a spirit tree .

There is also a Monkey nut bush under the Ape Atoll agility course, however this bush only grows Tchiki monkey nuts during Recipe for Disaster .

Monkey nuts is a colloquial term for peanuts. Unlike most other food, eating monkey nuts results in a message You eat the monkey nuts. even if the game messages are filtered. The message is the same regardless of whether it heals any health. This behaviour is shared with monkey bars and banana stew .

Ape Atoll is one of the most dangerous areas in the game. All native creatures other than the level 5 birds will be aggressive towards you, regardless of your combat level , whenever you're not wearing the monkey greegree (made later in the quest). Players can hug the coasts of Ape Atoll when moving to avoid the poisonous snakes and spiders; some snakes may still be encountered this way, but players can simply wait for them to move.

When going to the island, make sure to bring plenty of food , antipoison potions , and an emergency teleport , in addition to any other required items. Switching off auto retaliate and utilising protection prayers will greatly improve your chances of survival.

At any point, you can teleport or flee from Ape Atoll to restock items without losing your progress. To leave the island by boat, simply talk to Lumdo in the landing area to go from Ape Atoll back to Crash Island , and then talk to Waydar on Crash Island to go back to the Tree Gnome Stronghold . To resume the quest, talk to Daero on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree to go back to the hangar, talk to Waydar in the hangar to go back to Crash Island, and finally, talk to Lumdo on Crash Island to return to Ape Atoll.

results.section_path: General information > Access to Slayer masters
results.text:
In general, obtain tasks from the highest-level Slayer master that your Combat and Slayer levels allow. The monsters they assign generally give more experience than lower-level Slayer masters. Duradel is the best Slayer master to use for the fastest experience, but some players may find that Nieve 's (or Steve 's) task weighting better suit their preferences. Note that just because the player can access better Slayer masters, this does not directly translate to more experience per hour. That is, maximising experience per hour is not simply a matter of always taking tasks from the highest-level Slayer master that is currently available to the player.

Some players train Slayer using only one master. However, players typically train Slayer by switching between two masters. They do this by using one specific Slayer master that is appropriate for (or lower than) their level, and then switch to using a different higher-levelled Slayer master in order to take advantage of completion milestones. There are Slayer completion milestones for every 10th, 50th, 100th, 250th and 1000th task completion that award additional Slayer points. Higher-levelled masters will assign more difficult tasks than the typical Slayer master would, either in monster assigned or quantity given, but the reward is a greater bonus of Slayer points.

Each Slayer master usually assigns various monsters based on a weight rating, which determines how likely the player is to get that task. The latter three Slayer masters usually have a shared pool of assignable monsters, albeit with modifications to either the quantity or weighting.

Requirements or quests for accessing different Slayer masters and areas include:

Hastae are spears that may be used with a shield . The Zamorakian hasta on Stab works ideal against dragons and bosses, such as the Corporeal Beast . Similar to their two-handed brethren, spears, they are poison -able, except the Zamorakian hasta, and flexible, which means possessing the Stab , Crush , and Slash styles, and they also can only be used to train Controlled and Defensive attacks.

Claws are members-only slashing weapons that take up the shield and the weapon slot. The speed of claws are equal to that of daggers , and they have higher bonuses.

The abyssal whip is a very popular weapon among higher levels that is functionally similar to a scimitar in terms of speed, and has a high strength bonus. However, players cannot use the whip to train Strength effectively as it only has accurate , controlled , and defensive styles and lacks the aggressive attack style .

Axes are intended for Woodcutting and pickaxes for Mining . Although they may be used for melee combat, it is not recommended as the dragon axe and pickaxe are very expensive, and they have low speed and accuracy.

A stamina potion restores 20% of the player's run energy per dose, and offers a 70% reduction in run energy depletion for 2 minutes. This effect does not stack, and drinking additional doses before the timer has run out will simply reset it back to 2 minutes. When the stamina effect is active, the boost in the run energy orb changes from its usual yellow to orange.

A stamina potion can be made at level 77 Herblore by mixing a super energy potion with amylase crystals . Each dose grants 25.5 Herblore experience , and requires one amylase crystal.

At 85 Herblore, they can be used to make extended stamina potions using marlin scales .

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a stamina potion(2) to produce a stamina mix . This requires 86 Herblore and provides 60 Herblore experience. A stamina mix has 2 doses, each healing 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual stamina potion behaviour.

An energy potion restores 15% of the player's run energy per dose. It can be made at level 26 Herblore by mixing a harralander in a vial of water and then adding chocolate dust , granting 67.5 Herblore experience.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a 2 dose energy potion, which requires 29 Herblore and yields a 2 dose energy mix and 14 Herblore experience. An energy mix heals 3 hitpoints in addition to restoring 15% run energy.

It can be purchased from Apothecary's Potions in Varrock for 1 chocolate dust and 2 limpwurt roots , obtained from Dr Jekyll in exchange for a ranarr weed , or obtained as a common drop from various early game monsters, such as goblins , dark wizards , NPCs with the standard "human" drop table such as men , and low level Slayer monsters.

query: How do you defeat Zooknock in Monkey Madness I?

results.text:
| Mission Over

The jingle that plays upon defeating the jungle demon.

Once the Jungle Demon is slain, speak to Garkor, who is indicated by an arrow. He will tell you to speak to Zooknock; speak to Zooknock nearby to get the option to be teleported back to Ape Atoll. If players decline the offer and stay, they are free to explore the banana plantation , but Zooknock will leave, requiring players to speak to Bonzara instead if they want to be teleported. He can be found in the crack at the base of the statue.

Warning : The gnomes will teleport you into the jungle on Ape Atoll. It is advised to simply teleport off of the island as quickly as possible; players wishing to stay on the island should immediately equip their greegree after being teleported by the gnomes.

Escape the island however you like, either through the main gates as a monkey, with any form of teleport, or by jumping off the bridge in the south-east part of the city, and go back to the Gnome Stronghold .

Speak with King Narnode in the Grand Tree to finish the quest.

Congratulations, quest complete!

The king will then redirect you to Daero for your training as a new 10th squad member, so go have a chat with Daero for some optional experience rewards.

and drinking potions as needed. talk to zooknock to get an enchanted bar and your m'amulet mould back. do not use the m'amulet mould on zooknock when you already have the enchanted bar, otherwise he will keep it and you will have to obtain another.

Kill one of the Monkey Zombies and pick up the zombie monkey bones . Climb back up the rope, kill one of the Monkey Guards and pick up the gorilla bones . If you're having trouble with the guard, stay out of melee range so it doesn't heal.

If you're having trouble with the guard, stay out of melee range so it doesn't heal.

Speak with Garkor one more time (as a human or monkey) to receive a 10th squad sigil . Do not equip it until you are ready for the final battle . Make sure to hold onto the sigil, as if you lose it, Garkor will send you to Waymottin at the end of Zooknock 's tunnel to reclaim it.

Bank in preparation for the Jungle Demon fight, and ensure you have full prayer points and health. When you are ready to fight, wear the sigil, and you will be promptly teleported to the Jungle Demon's arena.

note:

You can wear the sigil, to start the fight, from anywhere in RuneScape; no need to return to Ape Atoll. Although you "wear" the sigil, it stays in your inventory and doesn't unequip your neck-slot equipment. Activate Protect from Magic before teleporting, and drink any necessary potions . Switch to your weapon/unequip your greegree before teleporting. You will lose your greegree if you have it equipped and your inventory is full when you teleport.

Upon landing in the arena, you'll be confronted by a level 195 Jungle Demon which can hit up to 32 with both magic and melee. Protection prayers reduce all damage to zero; as such, if the player stands out of melee range, the fight can be completed by simply leaving on Protect from Magic and attacking the demon with Magic or Ranged. Note that the demon's melee attack can hit you even if you're two squares away, similar to a halberd; ensure you're three or more squares away to avoid it. Additionally, standing still once you are teleported to the arena will keep a distance between you and the Demon, who will not move until you do, although it will still attack you with Magic.

Now is an ideal time to resupply at a bank before heading into the Ape Atoll Dungeon . Return to Ape Atoll by talking to Daero , Waydar , and Lumdo . Follow the yellow path west and climb down the ladder into the Ape Atoll Dungeon . Run to the end of the dungeon. Use Protect from Melee prayer and ignore all the hazards, eating food and drinking potions as needed. Talk to Zooknock . Use your Monkey dentures , M'amulet mould , and Gold bar on Zooknock . Talk to Zooknock to get an Enchanted bar and your M'amulet mould back. Do not use the m'amulet mould on Zooknock when you already have the enchanted bar, otherwise he will keep it and you will have to obtain another. Teleport away, then return by talking to Daero , Waydar , and Lumdo . Follow the red path, get arrested, escape, then follow the pink path to the temple. (Note: bearded guards cannot be walked through!) Enter the trapdoor . You may need to climb up the ladder to the south then down in the east to avoid the gorillas. With a M'amulet mould in your inventory, use the Enchanted bar with a wall of flames, then string it with your Ball of wool to create the M'speak amulet . Optional : If you plan on doing the Freeing King Awowogei section of Recipe for Disaster : Kill one of the Monkey Zombies and pick up the zombie monkey bones . Climb back up the rope, kill one of the Monkey Guards and pick up the gorilla bones . If you're having trouble with the guard, stay out of melee range so it doesn't heal.
